framing.headline: The metric that matters is ARAG contract value influenced, not standalone product ARR
framing.body: Across all three accelerators, the same conclusion holds independently: as standalone businesses these are feature-sized markets. Combined three-year SOM base case is roughly $1.9M ARR across all three products — real, but feature-sized, not company-sized. We are at the cheap end of every market we are in, and the monetisable unit is not usage.
framing.primaryMetric: Measure success in ARAG ACV (annual contract value) influenced and Knowledge Boxes provisioned, not in product ARR. The VoiceBridge report states the conclusion that applies to all three: measure success in ARAG ACV influenced, not in product ARR.

caveats: The market-size estimates in every category are definitionally broken, not empirically settled. IDP estimates span 8.5x depending on scope ($1.7bn Everest for IDP products alone versus $14.66bn MarketsandMarkets for "Document AI" including ECM); conversation intelligence shows a 42% spread between two analyst houses using the same market name (Mordor $4.01bn vs Fortune Business Insights $5.70bn for 2026); voice AI spans two orders of magnitude depending on whether "conversational AI" is defined to include chat (MarketsandMarkets $13.2bn including chat vs Grand View's $2.5-3.5bn for voice agents alone). In every case our bottom-up unit-economics check landed at or below the low end of the top-down range, so we plan on the bottom-up numbers.
Every figure in the underlying research carries a fetch date of 12 September 2026 and pricing in this category is volatile. Re-check any figure before it reaches a customer-facing deck.

Several vendor pages were unretrievable at research fetch time and are marked as such rather than filled in: Azure's marketing pricing page renders "$-" client-side (the Azure Retail Prices API was used instead), AWS Bedrock Data Automation per-page rates, Chunkr's client-rendered pricing, NICE's copilot product page (404), both Talkdesk copilot URLs (404), Google Agent Assist pricing, and the primary ARAG security page (403/404, with a secondary source cited and flagged in its place).

Private-company revenue figures (Gong, Cresta, Observe.AI, ElevenLabs, Sierra, Decagon) are secondary and unverifiable; they are labelled as such in the underlying research and none of them carries a sizing conclusion on its own.

The single biggest hole across all three sizing exercises: ARAG/Nuclia customer count is not publicly broken out anywhere. Progress has not disclosed how many customers or how much ARR Nuclia/ARAG represents, and every SAM/SOM line that depends on "reachable Progress/ARAG accounts" is therefore an assumption, not a sourced figure, pending internal Progress data.

arr.value: $852M at FY2025 Q4 end, +2% YoY constant currency; Q2 2026 update: $868M
arr.source: Progress Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 earnings releases (SEC 8-K exhibit 99.1)

nucliaAcquisition.value: Nuclia (Agentic RAG) acquired by Progress on 30 June 2025; consideration called immaterial by Progress

financials.notPublic: ARAG/Nuclia customer count, ARAG's ARR contribution to the $852M/$868M total, and per-product-line partner counts are not publicly disclosed by Progress.

products.name: Document Processing
products.topDownTam: $1.7bn (Everest Group, IDP products only, 2025, search-derived behind a paywall) to $14.66bn (MarketsandMarkets, "Document AI" including ECM, 2025) — an 8.5x spread explained by scope, not disagreement about the underlying market
products.cagr: ~33% (IDP-focused analyst houses: Grand View, Precedence, Global Market Insights) vs 13.5% (MarketsandMarkets, whose broader ECM-inclusive definition drags the average down) — evidence the two are measuring different things
products.bottomUpCheck: 30-180bn pages/year x $0.005-0.020/page blended realised price = $0.15-3.6bn/year, central estimate ~$0.75bn in 2026
products.verdictOnSpread: The bottom-up figure corroborates Everest's order of magnitude (~$1.7bn for IDP products) and flatly contradicts MarketsandMarkets, which would require a blended price of $0.195/page - twenty times Azure Layout's published $0.010/page rate. Rossum's $40,000/year for 100,000 pages ($0.40/page, ~40x Azure) explains essentially all of the 8.5x spread on its own: suite pricing vs API pricing for the same pages.
products.sam: ~$10-30M/year, dominated by the Progress channel and the regulated self-host segment
products.biggestHole: Nuclia/ARAG customer count is not publicly broken out - needs internal Progress data to replace the assumption that 0.2-1% of the API-layer TAM is reachable via the Progress channel

products.name: Call Analysis
products.topDownTam: ~$4-6bn (Mordor Intelligence $4.01bn (2026) vs Fortune Business Insights $5.70bn (2026), a 42% spread for the same market name, "speech analytics")
products.bottomUpCheck: Seats x attach rate x spend: 14m seats x 22% attach x $400/seat/year = ~$1.2bn (range $0.3-4.6bn). A minutes-based construction (945bn conversation minutes/year x share processed x price/minute) independently lands at $1.89bn at its central case, agreeing closely with the seats-based estimate.
products.verdictOnSpread: The software-only conversation-intelligence category is roughly $1-3bn; the $4-6bn top-down figures are services-inclusive. Two public incumbents (NICE $328M AI ARR, Verint $354M AI ARR) together disclose only about $0.68bn of AI-adjacent ARR against a claimed $4-6bn category, consistent with most of the category being services or bundled CCaaS revenue rather than a standalone software line.
products.sam: ~$20-120M/year of monetisable spend (support subscriptions, hosted instances, OEM embedding), against a $1-3bn software-only category
products.biggestHole: The no-SaaS seat share (assumed 1-3% of contact-centre seats) is unsourced, and it is not established that a $10-35k OSS annual-contract-value tier exists in this category at all - no vendor publishes a support-subscription price for an open-source conversation-intelligence product because no such product currently exists

products.name: VoiceBridge
products.topDownTam: Voice agents ~$2.5-3.5bn (2025-26, Grand View Research, secondary/search-derived, growing 25-39% CAGR); agent-assist ~$4-5bn (2025-26, Mordor Intelligence and public-filing cross-check, growing ~21% CAGR). Agent-assist is the primary market for VoiceBridge per the D-20 re-prioritisation to the Listen/live-brief use case.
products.bottomUpCheck: Voice agents: inverting analyst figures against Gartner's automation forecast gives ~$3bn - Gartner's stated 10% automation-by-2026 forecast is not realised in the arithmetic; the honest read is automation is still near Gartner's 2022-measured 1.6% baseline. Agent-assist: seats x attach x spend gives $0.67-6.0bn (14-20M seats x 10-25% attach x $360-1,200/seat/year).
products.verdictOnSpread: Agent-assist is larger and better-behaved than voice agents on every consistent reading, independently supporting the D-20 decision to prioritise the real-time listening / agent-assist use case over a voice-agent tool endpoint.
products.sam: ~$14-360M/year at an assumed $200-600/seat/year component price (below a full copilot price, since VoiceBridge is the context layer, not the UI)
products.biggestHole: The 14-20M contact-centre seat count rests on a single 2020 Synergy Research figure (29M agents at end-2019, cloud penetration under 20%); the copilot attach rate (10-25%) and the $360-1,200/seat/year spend range are both stated assumptions with no published comparable, not sourced figures

combined.interpretation: Every one of the three research documents reaches the same conclusion independently: as standalone businesses these are feature-sized markets, not company-sized ones. As attaches that help ARAG win regulated, grounded, self-hosted deals it would otherwise lose, they are well worth building - but the plan and the reporting should be built on ARAG contract value and Knowledge Box provisioning influenced, not on these ARR figures.
